changes_seen: Instruction: the explicit 'time left below nought' carve-out is gone. The silence clause now reads: work every figure out as the manual says, and keep only the step the code takes today to turn those figures into the reported value. That keep-step takes precedence over the no-guard sentence.
Instruction: the symptom list is rewritten, coverage now says 'entries of every status with and without miles', and time left is compared to within 0.001.

Manual 1.5 gains 'provides for logs as 1.1 to 1.3 describe them'. 2.2 is reworded to cover driving status plus yard moves. A new 2.3 defines a yard move as on-duty time in a stretch covering one mile or more. Later sections are renumbered 2.4-2.7 and the 1.3 cross-reference is updated.
README: the team-truck/co-driver explanation is removed. Miles is now 'recorded on every entry, whatever its status'.

limits.py: the loop now admits stretches that are driving or on-duty, and counts shift_on/today_on only for on-duty. Behaviour is unchanged for the shipped is_driving, but the structure now allows driving time that is not on-duty (a lure for miles-keyed yard moves).

prior_findings_status.note: The negative-time-left carve-out is no longer labelled. It now has to be derived from 1.5 plus the silence clause, and a second definitional trap (rest with miles is not a yard move, via 2.3 then 2.1) has been added. The screen now scores self_verification_resistance 3, which is at the build threshold. It is not a strong resist; see CR-7.

'still work out every figure that value is made from as the manual says, and keep only the step the code takes today to turn those figures into the reported value' names the conversion step. Limits, driving minutes, clock window and shift start all follow the manual. W6 is now determined: -0.0.
The new symptoms match the shipped code: 3.1 at 11h, window counted in on-duty minutes, shift-start-day attribution, and generous left (11h/70h, round, on-duty window).
'to within 0.001' is stated. -0.0 equals 0. Floor versus round differ by 0.1 or more wherever they differ, so the tolerance does not mask the trap.

The team explanation is gone. 2.3 keys yard moves on on-duty time and 1-mile stretches, so an `on` passenger stretch with miles is a yard move and off/sleeper with miles is not. Decidable from defined terms.

findings.issue: 5.2 ('Time left is reported in hours, rounded down to a tenth of an hour') reads as a positive, universal rule. Only 1.5's scoping sentence ('provides for ... time left from nought up to the limit') takes negative values out of its reach. This is decidable, because 1.5 limits what the manual provides for and the instruction's silence clause then applies. But it is a competing positive statement of the kind the 0/8 screen warns about: a reader who treats 1.5 as descriptive will floor negatives. It also has to be clear that 'below nought' is judged on the exact 5.1 value (-1 minute = -1/60 h) and not on the rounded one: floor would report -0.1, round reports -0.0.
findings.evidence: W6 (-1 min): -0.0 under keep-step, -0.1 under uniform floor. W11 (-8 min): -0.1 vs -0.2. W10 (-200 min): -3.3 vs -3.4. The two differ whenever |minutes| mod 6 is 1, 2 or 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional, and only if the builder wants lower fairness risk: make 5.2 say 'Time left, when the manual provides for it (1.5), is reported ...'. That strengthens the chain without naming the carve-out. If left as is, keep the verifier's negative-left cases (the 1, 2 and 3 minute residues) in the rubric's documented witnesses so the fairness reviewer can trace the 1.5 → silence-clause chain.

findings.location: design strength (instruction paragraph 2 wording; limits.py loop)
findings.issue: The redesign has one real trap and one weak one. (a) Negative time left keeps round(). The trap is real, but the silence clause is phrased so close to the answer ('keep only the step the code takes today to turn those figures into the reported value' plus a guard override) that a careful solver asking 'which reported value has no rule?' lands on 1.5 at once. (b) Rest with miles is not a yard move. The chain is 2.3 → 'on-duty time' → 2.1, but domain instinct (personal conveyance and berth time are off duty) points to the right answer, and the limits.py lure is weak against that. Under the platform calibration, (b) will rarely be missed, so the task effectively rests on one trap. A one-trap design gave CORE 4/8 once and 0/8 when every run missed it.
findings.evidence: Pre-mortem below. W9/W10 are right under both the 'status == on and miles >= 1' reading and the 'on-duty and miles >= 1' reading. Only a solver keying on miles alone fails, and the manual plus federal instinct both push against that.
findings.suggested_fix: No further redesign is allowed, so no core change. Make sure the verifier weights (a) across all three time-left keys with several residues, and covers (b) with off, sleeper and `on` stretches carrying 1+ miles. Do not add hints.

solver_path_screen.pre_mortem: A strong solver lists the departures, most of them unchanged from turn 1: constants, yard moves, rest-only breaks, on-duty shift start, clock window, own-day attribution, clock window-left, floor. It writes a per-minute reference from FM-4 and differential-fuzzes. Two reading decisions remain, and fuzzing cannot confirm either, because the solver's reference and patch share the same interpretation. (1) Yard move = 'on-duty time' with 1+ miles. The limits.py loop structure and 'miles recorded on every entry' invite keying on miles alone, but 2.3 → 2.1 plus federal instinct (personal conveyance and berth are off duty) lead most strong solvers to the correct `on`/`driving` reading. (2) Time left: the natural move is to replace round() with floor everywhere. Keeping round() for negatives needs the solver to connect 1.5's scope sentence to the silence clause. The clause is pointed ('keep only the step the code takes today to turn those figures into the reported value', plus a precedence override for guards), so a careful Opus 5.5 that asks 'which reported value has no rule?' will likely find it. A solver that reads 5.2 as universal, or treats 1.5 as boilerplate, floors negatives and fails every past-limit log whose residue is 1-3 minutes. That miss is the most likely one, and it lands across all three left keys.

score_notes.reference_unreachable: The manual is still a complete, executable spec for everything except the keep-step. The keep-step reference is the shipped hours() itself.
score_notes.authority_incomplete_for_grading: Negative time left is graded shipped behaviour inside a silent region, reached only by inference that self-testing cannot confirm. It is fair: the 1.5 chain plus the silence clause settle it.
score_notes.restraint_traps: One trap in the held shape: a silent sub-domain inside the same conversion step as a defect (round→floor), not labelled, reachable through the 1.5 definitional chain. One weak trap: rest with miles excluded via 2.3 → 2.1, which domain instinct already favours. Counted as roughly one and a half.
score_notes.fuzz_blind_spot: Past-limit logs and near-zero residues are generated naturally. The blind spot is interpretive, not a matter of input shape.

solver_path_screen.decisive_reason: Everything except negative-time-left rounding collapses to a from-manual reference. Whether a solver keeps round() there depends on one reading of 1.5 that fuzzing cannot confirm and that local Opus 5.5 will often, but not reliably, make.

overall_note: The contract is fair and determined. CR-2 to CR-5 are closed and nothing is reopened. The screen scores 3, which is the build threshold, so build. CR-6 (optional strengthening of the 5.2 scope) and CR-7 (verifier weighting across left keys and residues) are the fixes. Do not add hints that would disarm the 1.5 chain.
